page: Amazon Web Services g4dn.16xlarge is an accelerated computing instance built on the AWS Nitro System. It integrates a 64-vCPU Intel Xeon 8259CL processor running at 2.5 GHz across 32 physical cores, accompanied by 256 GB of DDR4 system memory. Hardware acceleration is provided by a single NVIDIA T4 GPU based on the Turing architecture with 16 GB of VRAM. Storage includes a dedicated 900 GB local NVMe SSD volume, complemented by 50 Gbps of baseline network bandwidth.

Benchmark results demonstrate specialized acceleration profiles. While single-thread processing reflects modest clock rates, resulting in lower scores on single-core stress-ng, gzip, and Geekbench suites, multi-core throughput remains steady across PassMark and compilation workloads. Large-block uncached memory read bandwidth reaches 210.38 GB/sec and write bandwidth reaches 93.59 GB/sec, placing it in the upper quartile. GPU-driven LLM prompt processing achieves top-tier throughput on small and medium models, delivering over 8,259 tokens per second on 135M models and 1,162 tokens per second on 7B models.

The platform offers a cost-effective hardware balance for organizations requiring GPU acceleration without scaling to high-end enterprise clusters. The integration of 256 GB system memory and local NVMe storage prevents bottlenecks during data staging. However, tasks bound strictly by single-thread CPU performance or 70B model sizes encounter hardware limits. It is well suited for machine learning inference, video transcoding, graphics workstation streaming, and mixed compute-storage pipelines.
description: Amazon Web Services g4dn.16xlarge is an accelerated computing instance powered by a 64-vCPU Intel Xeon 8259CL processor and a single NVIDIA Turing T4 GPU with 16 GB of VRAM. Configured with 256 GB of DDR4 memory, a bundled 900 GB local NVMe SSD, and 50 Gbps baseline networking, this Nitro-based system offers balanced resources for acceleration-heavy tasks. Benchmark data shows strong uncached memory bandwidth exceeding 210 GB/sec for reads and top-tier LLM inference prompt processing rates for small and medium parameter models. While single-core CPU throughput is comparatively modest, the combination of 32 physical cores, dedicated GPU hardware, and high-speed local storage delivers solid efficiency for machine learning inference, real-time video processing, graphics rendering, and data pipelines requiring GPU-assisted parallelization.
